summary:
## [1.3.5] - 2026-11-08

Release 1.3.5. Self-update on Windows completes instead of leaving the service stopped (a venue on 1.3.4 or older
installs this one by hand once, then updates itself), the release workflows take a capital-V tag and CI's format check
is green again, the phone's floor-plan view can be chosen in Settings, and a screenshot review of every screen on
desktop, tablet and phone fixed four visual faults.

### Fixed

- **Screen review, desktop and phone.** A screenshot pass over every staff, controller and admin screen at desktop,
  tablet and phone sizes found no overflow and no console errors, and four visual faults, all fixed: the "n TVs
  showing it" banner of the Where is the game? search drew over the header and the search box instead of inside the
  plan; the phone Audio tab's pinned master row was translucent, so the strips scrolling under it showed through;
  the master row's scenes divider opened a wrapped line on its own on a phone; and a long AdBreak chip ("Ad break ·
  house music · 2 s · back when the game resumes") ran off the full-screen zone page's header instead of truncating.
  The Audio pane's mix fold-out now puts each source on one line on a wide pane (name, fader, Mute, readout) instead
  of the phone's stacked shape.
- **The phone's floor-plan view was unreachable.** Settings › Phones › TVs tab › **View** offered only List and
  Grid, while the phone also has the floor plan pinned over the list, a dot per TV that finds its row and zone chips
  that keep one zone (the view the user guide already described). The select now offers it.
- **Self-update on Windows.** Admin › System › Software updates downloaded the installer and then sat on "Installing…
  the server restarts" with the service stopped, until someone ran the exe by hand. The server started the installer
  as a child of its own `node.exe`, and NSSM stops a service by killing its whole process tree, so the installer's
  first step, `net stop LTS-Control`, killed the installer itself before it had copied a file. The installer is now
  started through `cmd /c start`, which returns at once, so nothing links it to the service when it stops it; the
  five-minute timeout message quotes the installer's own `setup.log` too. The fix lives in the server that launches
  the update, so a Windows venue on 1.3.4 or older installs the next release by hand once, and updates itself from
  then on.
- **Release workflows and a capital-V tag.** A release tagged `V1.3.4` built the Windows installer but failed the
  Debian package ("a Debian version must start with a digit") and the update manifest ("not a version"), because
  the packages and manifest workflows stripped only a lowercase `v`. All three installer workflows now accept `v`,
  `V` and `v.` and refuse any other tag at their first step with a message that says what to do. A stray
  `test-results/.last-run.json` committed at the repository root is removed and ignored: it failed CI's format check
  on every run since it landed.
